speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis results are negative for bacteria, blood, leukocyte esterase, and nitrites, which makes a standard urinary tract infection unlikely. Since the specific gravity is normal and there is no proteinuria or glucose, do you have any urgency, nocturia (waking up at night to urinate), or difficulty starting your stream?

REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis is completely normal, which rules out a typical infection. With the ultrasound pending, do you experience leakage when you cough, sneeze, or laugh, or do you feel a strong, sudden urge to urinate that you cannot delay?

REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history; the combination of bladder discomfort, frequency, nocturia, dyspareunia, and relief with voiding strongly suggests a painful bladder syndrome or interstitial cystitis. Given your age and symptoms, have you noticed any visible blood in your urine, or has this condition run in your family?

REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy with hydrodistension
REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms of chronic bladder discomfort, frequency, nocturia, and dyspareunia, combined with a negative urinalysis and ultrasound, are highly suggestive of painful bladder syndrome (interstitial cystitis). To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other pathologies, do you see any blood in your urine?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Painful Bladder Syndrome (Interstitial Cystitis)
